analysis: What changed vs Monday's 9 AM brief: the tape flipped from historic rally to orderly giveback. Monday closed with the S&P +4.73% (7,237.17), Nasdaq +6.51% (24,089.56) and Dow +3.01% — the best day since April 2025 — on Huang's reinstatement, but Tuesday premarket futures slid steadily through the morning (S&P -0.23% at 4:30 AM ET to about -1% by 7 AM ET; Nasdaq-100 -0.61% to about -1.8%), led by the same chips that led Monday: NVDA -5%, AMD -4.4%, Intel -6-7%, Micron -7%. The giveback is concentrated, not broad — Dow futures are only -0.4 to -0.5% — which reads as profit-taking plus a re-pricing of the unresolved Huang overhang (SEC accounting probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony) rather than a fresh negative catalyst. HPE is the day's tell on AI hardware: a genuine beat-and-raise (revenue +50%, FY27 guide lifted sharply) still sold off ~10% premarket after +17% Monday, because the Q1 guide landed just under the rosiest Street estimates — the bar for AI server names is now the guide, not the quarter. Zoom is the quiet counterpoint: a beat, a first dividend and a raised profit guide, plus a $3.8B Anthropic stake now worth ~15% of its market cap, and the stock is flat. Regulatory flow is running both ways: the US blacklisted Alibaba's Singapore unit and Nvidia-linked Megaspeed over alleged chip diversion (BABA -2.8%), while Sanofi's $41B Insmed deal is the biggest biotech transaction in nearly three years. Overnight, Asian chip markets rallied hard (Taiwan Taiex ~+9%), so the US premarket fade is a US-session phenomenon, not a global reversal. Signal vs noise: the concentration of the pullback in Monday's winners and the steady widening of futures losses through the morning are signal — this is a digestion day; the exact premarket percentages are noise in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape, and today's macro (consumer confidence, FOMC minutes) plus Dell/HP after the close are the next real tests.

headlines.headline: Futures give back part of Monday's historic rally: at 6:03 AM ET, S&P 500 futures -0.79%, Nasdaq-100 futures -1.68%, Dow futures -0.39% — and losses widened through the morning (S&P about -1.0%, Nasdaq about -1.8% by ~7 AM ET). Monday closed S&P +4.73% to 7,237.17, Nasdaq +6.51% to 24,089.56, Dow +3.01% to 49,595.31, the best day since April 2025.
headlines.why_it_matters: The fade is concentrated in Monday's winners rather than broad — a digestion day after a record rally, but the steady widening through the morning shows sellers, not just profit-taking at the open.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -5% premarket (~$156.76 vs Monday's $165.05 close) after surging 31.5% Monday, its biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value. Chips broadly lower premarket: AMD -4.4%, Intel -6.3 to -7%, Micron -7%, Marvell -5.5%, ARM -5.1%. Investors are weighing multiple ongoing investigations around freshly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang (SEC accounting probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony).
headlines.why_it_matters: The leadership vacuum is closed, but the investigations that shadowed Huang's exit are still open — the market is re-pricing that overhang after Monday priced only the return.

headlines.headline: HPE beat and raised, and still fell: fiscal Q4 revenue $14.5B (+50% y/y), adjusted EPS $1.43 vs $1.28 consensus; FY27 revenue guidance raised to $59.4-63.1B (27-35% growth) and adjusted EPS to $5.05-5.35, free cash flow at least $5.5B, plus a $5B buyback authorization and a dividend raise to $0.17. Shares -9.6% premarket after +17% Monday, as the Q1 guide ($14.0-14.6B) came in just under the highest Street estimates. CEO Neri said HPE is not financing neocloud or high-risk customers to buy AI servers.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise selling off shows the bar for AI server names is now the guide, not the quarter — and the neocloud-financing comment draws a line under the riskiest corner of AI infrastructure demand.

headlines.headline: Zoom Q3 fiscal 2027: revenue $1.29B (+4.9% y/y), Enterprise revenue $805.4M (+8.6%, fastest in 13 quarters), adjusted EPS $1.59 vs $1.53 consensus; board started a first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.25 (payable Dec 17) and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.24-6.25. Zoom's early-2023 Anthropic investment is now estimated at ~$3.8B, about 15% of Zoom's market cap. Shares about flat (+0.13%) premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat, a first dividend and a raised profit guide — plus a $3.8B Anthropic stake — and the stock barely moves, showing how much of Tuesday's tape is about the chip giveback, not single-name fundamentals.

headlines.headline: Alibaba -2.8% premarket after the US Commerce Department added its Singapore unit (Apex Enterprise Solutions) and Nvidia-linked cloud firm Megaspeed to the Entity List on Monday over alleged AI chip diversion to China; seven entities across Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand were added, with licenses under a presumption of denial. Alibaba denies the allegations and plans a legal challenge; Singapore says it is still investigating Megaspeed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Export-control enforcement is now hitting listed-company subsidiaries, not just obscure intermediaries — a direct overhang on Alibaba and a reminder the chip-diversion probe still touches Nvidia's partner network.

headlines.headline: Sanofi agreed to buy US biotech Insmed for $41B in cash ($175/share), a ~17% premium to Monday's close and ~46% to the Nov 18 close before deal reports — the biggest biotech deal in nearly three years. Insmed +14% premarket. The deal adds two commercial respiratory drugs (Brinsupri, Arikayce) and a phase 3 asset, is expected to be EPS-accretive by end of 2028, and is expected to close in H1 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: A $41B cash deal on a quiet premarket morning shows M&A appetite is alive even in a volatile tape — and it is a direct read on pharma paying up for respiratory assets ahead of Dupixent's patent cliff.

headlines.headline: AMD filed an S-3 registering up to 336.9M shares for potential resale by existing shareholders and strategic partners, covering shares tied to its OpenAI and Meta agreements and its World Labs and Taalas acquisitions. AMD is not selling the shares itself and receives no proceeds. Shares -3.2% premarket after closing nearly 7% higher Monday.
headlines.why_it_matters: No new shares are being issued, but a large resale registration from strategic partners reads as potential supply overhang — enough to weigh on a stock that ran 7% the day before.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) shares briefly crossed below their $83 IPO price in premarket trading, after sitting out Monday's rally at around $88 (-1% on the day). Friday's close was $88.91.
headlines.why_it_matters: The newest mega-IPO is still not joining the relief rally and is now testing its IPO price — buyers remain selective even on a record up day.

headlines.headline: Oil eased despite a Strait of Hormuz incident: Brent -0.84% to $88.62 and WTI -0.74% to $79.58 at 4:30 AM ET, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three oil tankers it described as violating caught fire after hitting naval mines in the strait on Monday. Supply and surplus concerns outweighed the shipping risk.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even tankers hitting mines in the Strait is not lifting crude — the market is pricing surplus over geopolitics, which keeps energy a drag on the tape rather than a haven.
